doc.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022

title: Playing with Sun Ra
summary: Blue auditions for Sun Ra's band, learns from John Gilmore to play without charts, and takes from Sun Ra that music is not about money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: All right. Let me ask you about a few of the people you’ve performed with. Sun Ra?
What can you share with us about Sun Ra?

Sunny was very interesting man. Sunny, it was an important time for me to meet Sunny and to — I actually auditioned to play with his group. It was a brief time but it was a time, it was amazing. He’s a remarkable musician and a remarkable spirit. He has a concept that still lives today even though he’s not here so there is something really really special and important about him. Playing in that band, well let’s see, that’s where I met John Gilmore as well and a quick story, I was the newbie in the band and I’m there waiting, because we rehearsed and we were reading charts and stuff. Okay. I didn’t have any charts when we got to the gig. I’m the only one in the section and I’m looking around, the cats are ignoring me and I’m saying oh man, okay here we go. And Gilmore was watching me and finally he said, he said, “Look man, don’t worry about it I got ya.” I didn’t know what that was supposed to mean. But the point of it was when the gig started there were no charts. So what I did was I listened, I paid very close attention to John, how he handled the situation. And yeah, you had to have your big ears on you know, because your role was to contribute and blend in a way that Sunny needed you to blend. Like he would just point to you and then you’d play. And I’m saying to myself what do I play? The guy said, “Play!” “Play what?” “Play, man.” I said, “Okay.” So yeah, so Marshall Allen, I was checking out Marshall and Sunny and a bunch of the other cats. And Gary Bartz was in that band at that time. He was there as well. And so the cats turned and looked at me with smiles I said I guess I’m doing the right thing man. So yeah. But that was an amazing experience. And Sunny had pulled me aside. And he was getting ready to do a video project. He says, “I got something for you, I want you to be a part of this.” But it didn’t happen. It didn’t come to fruition because he had passed away. I didn’t know he wasn’t well at the time, but yeah that didn’t happen. But that’s how that was. Yeah.

That’s a great memory. And I had the pleasure of talking with Marshall Allen and he’s quite a spirit. At the end he said something like I’ve been doing this for fifty years I’m still waiting to make some money.

Yeah. Well money wasn’t the center, play with Sunny. No. Forget that. But the music and the vibe and the people, the experience, that was it. And what I learned from him is that you know it’s not all about money. It’s just what are you going to learn from this? You know? How are you going to become better as a person, as a musician, just a better being
from being a part of this? That’s what we have to look for. You know? That’s what I got from Sun Ra’s band.
